subject: Request for SLA credit & uptime apportionment for Oct 12 maintenance window
messages:
From: John Doe <john.doe@edgechain.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Rafael Mendes <rafael.mendes@redwood.com>
Cc: ops@edgechain.com
Date: 2026-10-15T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request for SLA credit: Oct 12 partial degradation during scheduled maintenance?

Hi Marissa / Rafael,

Thanks for the quick sync earlier. Following up with the official request for an SLA credit tied to the partial degradation we observed on Oct 12 during what your status page labelled as a "scheduled maintenance window". We experienced elevated error rates and increased tail latency across several endpoints between 02:18 and 03:50 UTC — we've attached our internal edge metrics and a short postmortem.

EdgeChain's postmortem (attached) indicates a third-party CDN performed an overlapping maintenance that they now say was pre-scheduled, but the timing partially overlapped with Redwood's maintenance window and also had independent failover impact. Our contract language around uptime apportionment asks for clarification on how you attribute overlapping maintenance vs third-party incidents.

Can you confirm:
- Whether Redwood will exclude the full window as customer-initiated maintenance,
- Or whether Redwood will apportion the outage and grant credit for the portion attributable to your service (not the third party),
- If apportionment is the approach, please share the calculation and supporting logs.

We'd like to close the credit request this week. Please see attached: edgechain-postmortem.pdf and uptime-report-oct12.csv.

Best,
John
John Doe
Site Reliability Lead, EdgeChain
ops@edgechain.com

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Request for SLA credit: Oct 12 partial degradation during scheduled maintenance?

On Fri, Oct 15, 2026 at 10:03 AM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Team — looping you in to assess. Key asks from EdgeChain: whether to treat the entire overlap as our maintenance, or to apportion credit for the portion of degradation caused by our runtime. Rafael, I copied you since you own maintenance scheduling policy; Marcus, can you run the initial apportionment against our token/route metrics and share a short write-up and numbers?

Attached is a draft apportionment (uptime-apportionment-draft.xlsx) and a slice of the route-level probes. Summary of my findings:
- Our scheduled maintenance window: Oct 12 02:00–04:00 UTC.
- Customer observed elevated error rates: 02:18–03:50 UTC.
- Third-party CDN reported maintenance 02:30–02:55 UTC and a concurrent failover event at 02:47–03:05 UTC.

My read: there are three zones to consider — pre-third-party impact (02:18–02:30), overlap (02:30–03:05), and post-third-party tail (03:05–03:50).
- Pre-third-party (02:18–02:30): attributable to our maintenance (full creditable window if we consider maintenance as customer-affecting).
- Overlap (02:30–03:05): mixed causality. Our probes show partial degradation independent of CDN for some routes; other routes show CDN-originated errors. I propose apportioning this window 50/50 (Redwood/third party) for credit purposes unless legal/sales prefer a different split.
- Post-third-party (03:05–03:50): mostly third-party tail; limited impact on our runtime but still customer-visible. I propose we exclude this tail from our maintenance credit (i.e., not grant credit for it) but provide mitigation notes.

If we go with the 50/50 overlap split, the resulting customer-facing credit is ~0.42% of the monthly uptime for Oct (calc in spreadsheet). If we instead treated the whole 02:00–04:00 as our maintenance, we would deny a credit — that will not land well with EdgeChain given their independent telemetry.

Attachments: uptime-apportionment-draft.xlsx (spreadsheet), uptime-report-oct12.csv (customer-supplied sample).

Marcus Lin
Director, Runtime Reliability, Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com

Forwarded message:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-10-18T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Proposed response & credit for EdgeChain (Oct 12)
To: John Doe <john.doe@edgechain.com>

Hi John — thanks for the patience while we looked into this. Below is our proposal and the rationale; please review and let us know if it resolves the request.

Summary (proposed):
- We agree to a partial credit for Oct 12 covering the window 02:18–03:05 UTC.
- Apportionment: Redwood will accept 60% of responsibility for the overlap window (02:30–03:05) and 100% for the pre-overlap window (02:18–02:30). We will not grant credit for the post-CDN tail (03:05–03:50) because telemetry indicates the residual impact was dominated by the third party.
- Credit calculation: one-time invoice credit equal to 0.56% of the Oct invoice (detailed calc attached).
- Next steps: we will schedule a postmortem sync with EdgeChain SREs and our CDN vendor to align on coordinated maintenance signaling.

Rationale: Marcus' probe work shows mixed causality in the overlap window. Given the customer's independent telemetry, a 60/40 split is a fair compromise that preserves our maintenance scheduling policy and demonstrates good faith.

If you approve the wording, I'll send the formal credit email and route the invoice credit via finance. Linking INF-982 for internal tracking.

Regards,
Stephanie Nguyen
Director, Customer Success Operations, Redwood Inference
stephanie.nguyen@redwood.com

---
Approved? Reply-all with sign-off. If no reply by EOD tomorrow, I'll proceed with the customer communication and finance ticket (INF-982).
